title: Ring Card intermediate program
description: The contract between the extractor (parse.py) and the renderer (render.js). Faithful extract of one judging program. Everything here is a FACT read off the PDF. Derived values (estimated times, clash flags) are NOT stored here — the renderer computes them from slotMin + ahead + weekend.json estimates so retuning re-derives everything.

entries.description: Every breed judged that day, in program order within each ring/time-block. The renderer filters to the breeds named in weekend.json.

breed.description: Breed name exactly as printed, e.g. 'Finnish Spitz'

ring.description: Physical ring number from the ring-detail header (NOT the alphabetical summary)

judge.description: Judge from the ring-detail header (already reflects substitutions)

slotMin.description: slotTime as minutes since midnight, e.g. 650

ahead.description: Sum of dogs in the same ring+time-block listed BEFORE this breed. 0 = first in the block.

prevBreed.description: Breed immediately before this one in the block (the ringside cue). null if first.

prevN.description: Entry count of prevBreed. null if first.

split.description: Regular Dogs-Bitches-BOB(d)-BOB(b), e.g. '0-0-2-0'. null when not printed (e.g. puppy/junior).

puppy.description: 4-6mo Beginner Puppy or similar side event

flags.description: Parser confidence notes, e.g. 'low-confidence-time'. Present only when the extractor was unsure — tells the human which fields to check by hand.

ring.description: Physical ring the group judging runs in. Regular and NOHS each get their own — often different rings.

follows.description: NOHS-only: true when timing is 'Immediately following each Regular Variety Group' rather than a printed clock time.

order.description: Groups in printed order. Position in this array is the group's running order (1st, 2nd, ...).
